vm_tools: concierge: do not keep xattrs/fflags in VM exports When exporting VMs, do not attempt to store extended attributes or "fflags" (chattr-style attributes). The files that are being archived should be normal files, aside from having the "encrypted" chattr flag set, which can't be preserved in an archive anyway. When libarchive adds files with these flags to a PAX-style tar file, it creates extra sections that GNU tar doesn't understand, which results in confusing error messages when extracting the tarball. Disable them to avoid adding the extra sections when using libarchive's "restricted pax" format so that the resulting tar file is cleanly extract-able with GNU tar and other tar implementations. platform_ServoPowerStateController: make dut_off detection EC dependent Currently, this test asserts whether a DUT is off by pinging it and hoping for no response. This is noisy, but more importantly, it doesn't actually answer the question whether the DUT is off, but rather whether it responds to pings. dlcservice: Maintain cache state of dlc roots Dlcservice will maintain the dlc roots alongside the installed DLC(s). During |LoadDlcModuleImages()|, it is already the case that if a mounting fails then the failed DLC will not end up in |installed_dlc_modules_|, so |LoadDlcModuleImages()| will only add to the |installed_dlc_modules_| DLC(s) that are installed with mount. During |Install()|, no change is made to |installed_dlc_modules_|. During |Uninstall()|, we only remove from |installed_dlc_modules_| if unmounting and deleting both succeed (neither unmount nor delete should ever fail, but in the case that they do, it will lead dlcservice into an unstable state). Deleting al already deleted file or directory returns true and will not fail, which desired behavior. During |OnStatusUpdateAdvancedSignal()| most of the work happens. Dlcservice goes through the DLC(s) that finished installing and need to be mounted. Only when all the `to be` installed DLC(s) are mounted, do they go into the |installed_dlc_modules_| with there corresponding dlc roots. network_WiFi_LinkMonitorFailure: don't fail upon lack of disconnect This test is testing to ensure (a) Shill's link monitor detects a link failure (e.g., failing ARP requests) within a certain timeout and (b) the rest of the stack (driver, wpa_supplicant) responds appropriately when Shill requests a WiFi Reattach() Reattach() is just a "Reassociation attempt": https://w1.fi/wpa_supplicant/devel/dbus.html#dbus_interface which traditionally resulted in a disconnect/reconnect, but is now widened such that some drivers support the reassociation attempt directly, and therefore do not yield any disconnect. See https://crbug.com/990012#c4 for some more information about this. Anyway, the result is the 'iw event' only shows the "connected" event, with no disconnect in the meantime. This was confirmed in a WiFi sniffer packet capture. Since this behavior doesn't really violate (b), we should loosen this restriction, and avoid failing the test just because we didn't see a disconnect. A Reassociation should be as good as a Deauth/Reassociation in terms of "un-sticking" the driver. dev-lang/rust: use llvm-libunwind as the unwinder This uses the statically linked llvm-libunwind as Rust's unwinder instead of the dynamically linked one from gcc_s. This adds about 30k to the binary size but rust binaries will no longer depend on gcc_s. This change required an upstream patch to make it build with cross-compilation. The libunwind code was missing from from the llvm fork shipped with the rustc source tarball for unknown reasons. The ebuild sources the llvm fork directly from github and places the libunwind source in the correct spot. Because gcc_s isn't linked, a latent bug in mosys's link step was seen on armv7 builds. There was a missing compiler builtin that gcc_s provided that is no longer there. This was fixed in this CL by including the default libs via `-C default-linker-libraries`, which pulls in LLVM's compiler_rt. See crbug.com/868726 for more details about the issue. net-print/ippusbxd: Adding exponential backoff for print read requests Initiating read requests uses an asynchronous callback system where requests are sent to the printer and then a callback will fire with the printer's response. If the printer currently has no data to service the read request then it responds with a 0-byte message. This system lead to ippusbxd spamming the printer continuously with read requests that came back with empty responses. This change introduces exponential backoff so that if an empty response is received from the printer, ippusbxd will wait for increasingly long periods before issuing another request. This change significantly reduces syslog spam, and should result in faster communication with the printer. shill: connection: Add oif rules for all interfaces Previously, a pair of iif rules were added for all physical interfaces. However, this still left an edge case in which a socket has SO_BINDTODEVICE but does not have bind() explicitly called. In this case, at connect() time, the socket is still implicitly bound to INADDR_ANY (for AF_INET sockets), and source address selection must occur. However, lacking any oif rules, our set of policy rules has nothing to distinguish this source address selection case from regular source address selection. Therefore when the socket is bound to a device that is not the primary interface on the system, the bound device and the outcome of source address selection are in disagreement. This change adds a pair of oif rules for all interfaces so that source address selection takes any potential bound device into account. Adding this functionality required providing support for FRA_OIFNAME in shill. Note that all of our kernel trees define this routing policy type. uhid: fix a race condition in closing device There was an error ERR newblued[2999]: E@ uhid.c:472: No devInfo found which was caused by a race condition between freeing a HID device and destroying the corresponding kernel device. This simple patch fixed the problem by freeing the device only after receiving the kernel UHID_CLOSE output event. BUG=chromium:977106 TEST=Pair and remove a BLE mouse. Observe that the "No devInfo found" errors were not seen any more.
